targetText: Wanting to abolish authority in large-scale industry is tantamount to wanting to abolish industry itself, to destroy the power loom in order to return to the spinning wheel.
summary: Modern industrial production requires technical coordination and subordination to mechanical processes regardless of social form.
explanation: Engels demonstrates that modern large-scale production, driven by complex machinery and interconnected processes, physically imposes coordination and scheduled labor upon producers. Demanding the abolition of all authority in production would require abolishing modern industry itself and regressing to primitive handicraft production.

targetText: But the necessity of authority, and of imperious authority at that, will nowhere be found more evident than on board a ship on the high seas. There, in time of danger, the lives of all depend on the instantaneous and absolute obedience of all to the will of one.
summary: Collective survival and complex navigation require disciplined delegation of operational authority.
explanation: Engels illustrates through maritime navigation that complex logistical operations require clear chains of execution and instantaneous obedience in times of peril. Replacing functional leadership with individual vetoes or endless deliberation during crises guarantees collective catastrophe.

targetText: Hence it is absurd to speak of the principle of authority as being absolutely evil, and of the principle of autonomy as being absolutely good. Authority and autonomy are relative things whose spheres vary with the various phases of the development of society.
summary: Authority and autonomy are relative social relations defined by historical conditions rather than moral absolutes.
explanation: Engels rejects the metaphysical view that treats authority as an absolute evil and individual autonomy as an absolute good. In Marxist dialectics, authority and autonomy are relational concepts that transform alongside technological development, social division of labor, and mode of production.

targetText: A revolution is certainly the most authoritarian thing there is; it is the act whereby one part of the population imposes its will upon the other part by means of rifles, bayonets and cannon : authoritarian means, if such there be at all; and if the victorious party does not want to have fought in vain, it must maintain this rule by means of the terror which its arms inspire in the reactionists.
summary: A socialist revolution is inherently authoritarian because it forcibly suppresses the capitalist class to protect working-class power.
explanation: Engels delivers his classic critique of anarchist anti-authoritarianism: a revolution does not dissolve authority into thin air, but forcibly wields armed power to overthrow the ruling class and suppress capitalist counter-revolution. Rejecting state authority immediately after revolution disarms the proletariat and delivers victory back to the bourgeoisie.
